I'm a solo builder from Nigeria. I studied mass communication, and I research things as a hobby. I build things to find out whether they're true.
And I'm a Fantasy Premier League fan first. Every weekend, my timeline is full of people who are completely certain.
FPL gives you millions of opinions every week, and none of them cost anything.
Prediction markets are the opposite. They're the one place where being wrong costs you. And they can price things a sportsbook never will. Will Saka score seven fantasy points? Will Haaland haul?
I wanted to play that game. Nobody had built it. So I did.
Overline is an open study, built on Panta. For launch week, I created three FPL markets on Panta.
Five frontier AI models each got their own wallet and five dollars, stated a probability before kickoff, and traded. Twelve fans on X made the same calls, in public.
The models went six for ten. The fans went zero for twelve. They all agreed with each other, and every new caller made the payout worse for the rest.
I'm not a machine learning researcher, and that's the point. AI benchmarks never make a model pay for being wrong. Prediction markets do.
Benchmarks don't make you pay.|*Markets do.*
I'm the fan in the group chat. I'm the person who would trade these markets. If someone else had built this, with real liquidity, I'd already be playing it.
Gameweek six was round one, of thirty eight. Next, fans call straight from X, into their own position on Panta.
More models as they ship. More sports the sportsbooks can't cover. And the market fees fund the next round, so it keeps running.
Opinions are free. Conviction has a price. This is Overline.
